shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only A for another B would leave me with 0 A and 2 B, creating imbalance and reducing variety, which lowers my utility given my preference for balanced holdings.

Currently I have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only B for another A would leave me with 2 A and 0 B, reducing variety and utility since I value diversity across goods. This trade doesn't improve my bundle.

Currently I have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, C, which is my ideal balanced state. Trading away my only B for 2 A would leave me with 3 A, 0 B, 1 C - a highly unbalanced bundle that reduces variety value despite increasing total goods. I'd rather seek a trade that maintains or improves balance.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only C for another B would leave me with 0 C and 2 B, creating imbalance and reducing variety, which lowers my utility given my preference for balanced holdings.

Trading my 1 B for 1 C would leave me with 1 A, 0 B, 2 C - reducing variety since I'd have zero of a good instead of an even spread of 1-1-1. Since I equally value goods but prefer variety, this trade decreases my utility rather than increasing it. I'd rather keep my balanced inventory or find a trade that doesn't zero out a good.

Current inventory is 1/1/1, perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for 2 C would leave me with 1 A, 0 B, 3 C — creating a scarcity of B and excess of C, which reduces variety and hurts my utility despite the quantity gain.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only A for another B would leave me with 0 A, 2 B, 1 C, which reduces variety and lowers my utility since I value diversity across goods.
I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only B for another A would make me have 2 A's and 0 B's, reducing variety and utility rather than improving it.

Current inventory is balanced at 1-1-1, which I value for variety. Trading away my only B for 2 A would leave me with 3 A and 0 B, creating a lopsided bundle (concentrating in a good I already have) and eliminating a good entirely - this reduces variety and utility rather than increasing it.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my C for another B would make my bundle 1 A, 2 B, 0 C, reducing variety and leaving me with zero C, which lowers my utility given my preference for balanced diversity.

This trade would give me 2×C and 0×B, moving me from a balanced (1,1,1) bundle to an unbalanced (1,0,2) bundle. Since I value variety, going to zero of a good decreases utility more than gaining a second C increases it. I'd rather keep my current even distribution or find a trade that doesn't create a zero-holding.

Current inventory is 1/1/1, perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for 2 C would leave me with 1 A, 0 B, 3 C, creating imbalance and reducing variety value, which hurts my utility since I value even distribution.

Currently I have 1 A, 0 B, 1 C. Trading away my only A for B gives me a bundle of 0A,1B,1C, which is still varied but I lose A entirely. Actually better: after trade I'd have A:0, B:1, C:1 - equal variety across two goods but zero of A. Since I value variety and currently have zero B (lowest holding), acquiring B increases utility more than losing my single A costs, since I'd end up with two goods at 1 each instead of an uneven 1,0,1. This equalizes my holdings and improves diversity, so accepting increases utility."

Currently I have A:1, B:0, C:1. Trading away my only C for a B gives me A:1, B:1, C:0, which is still a balanced variety bundle with no zero surplus in a good I need more of, and moves me toward a more even distribution since I lack B entirely. This maintains equal diversity while satisfying the variety preference just as well as before, so it's a neutral-to-positive trade given B's rising value in the market.

I currently have 3 A, 0 B, 1 C, a very unbalanced bundle. Trading 1 A (which I have plenty of) for 1 B (which I have none of) increases variety and balances my holdings, improving my utility under diminishing marginal value for goods I already hold in excess.

Current inventory is A:3, B:0, C:1. Giving up 2 A for 1 B would leave me A:1, B:1, C:1 which is actually a very balanced bundle - but giving away 2 A for only 1 B is a steep price. A better trade would be 1 A for 1 B, achieving similar diversification without overpaying. I'll reject this and counter with a more favorable ratio.

Trading away my only C would leave me with 0 C and 1 B, still a 2-good imbalance (A:3,B:1,C:0). Currently I have A:3,B:0,C:1 - going to A:3,B:1,C:0 doesn't improve variety balance since I'd still have a zero holding. Better to seek a trade that reduces my A surplus instead of eliminating my only C.

I currently have 3 A and 0 B or C, so trading 1 A (which I have plenty of) for 1 B (which I have none of) directly improves my variety-driven utility. This moves me toward a more balanced bundle, which is exactly what I value.
Giving up 2A for 1B is too steep - going from 3A/0B/0C to 1A/1B/0C leaves me with only 2 total goods and heavily imbalanced. I'd rather negotiate a 1-for-1 trade to build variety more efficiently.

Trading away my only A (which I have only 1 of) for B (which I have 0 of) would leave me with 0 A and 1 B, just shifting scarcity rather than improving variety. Currently I have 1A, 0B, 3C - giving up my sole A unit for B doesn't improve balance since I'd go from (1,0,3) to (0,1,3), still having a zero. I'd prefer to acquire B using C instead, since I have plenty of C to spare.

I currently have 0 B and 3 C, so trading away a C (which I have plenty of) for a B (which I have none of) improves variety and balances my bundle toward A:1, B:1, C:2 - a clear utility gain given my preference for diversity.

But giving up 2C for only 1B is steep since C is my most abundant good, but I'd rather negotiate a better ratio like 1C for 1B given B is in demand and valuable to me too. This trade would give me 2×A and 0×B, moving me from a balanced (1,1,0) inventory to an unbalanced (2,0,0). Since I value variety, reducing B to zero while increasing A (already equal) decreases my utility rather than improving it. I'd prefer trades that add C or maintain balance.

This trade would leave me with 3A, 0B, 0C - losing all variety in B and C, which is bad given my preference for balanced holdings. Giving up my only B for more A (which I already have) reduces diversity when I should be seeking C instead.

Currently I have A:1, B:1, C:0. Trading 1B for 1C gives me A:1, B:0, C:1 - moving from having two goods at 1 and one at 0 to still two at 1 and one at 0, but now I have variety across A and C instead of duplicate B, and since C was previously zero, gaining it increases marginal value more than losing a B I already had one of. This diversifies my holdings, which aligns with my preference for variety.

Giving up my only B (going to 0) to get 2 C would leave me with A:1, B:0, C:2 - losing variety in B entirely. I'd rather keep at least one of each good. A better trade would be giving something I have more of, or trading fewer B for C while keeping some B.

Currently I have A:2, B:0, C:1 - very unbalanced. Trading away 1 A (which I have plenty of) for 1 B (which I have none of) moves me toward A:1, B:1, C:1, a perfectly balanced bundle. This clearly increases my utility given my preference for variety.
Giving up 2A for 1B would leave me with 0A, 1B, 1C - going from balanced variety to zero in one good is worse. I'd prefer a 1-for-1 trade instead to gain B while keeping some A.

My inventory would become A:2, B:1, C:0, which is no better balanced than now. I'd rather keep C and seek a trade that adds B without losing my only C, or find better terms."
I have 2 A and 0 B or C. Trading 1 A for 1 B gives me a more diversified bundle (1 A, 1 B), which increases utility given my preference for variety.

Giving up 2A for only 1B would leave me with 0A, 1B, 0C - reducing my A holdings entirely while only gaining 1 unit of B. This is an unfavorable trade ratio; I'd rather trade 1A for 1B to diversify without losing all my A.

Giving up 2A for 1B would leave me with 0A, 1B, 1C - trading a scarce-ish good position for too little. Current bundle A:2,B:0,C:1; getting 1B while losing 2A over-concentrates my loss. I'd prefer a more balanced trade like 1A for 1B to diversify without giving up too much A.

Currently I have A:2, B:0, C:1. Trading away my only C for B would leave me with A:2, B:1, C:0, just shifting the imbalance from B to C rather than improving variety. Since I value variety, I'd prefer to keep C and instead acquire B without giving up my only C, or find a trade that improves diversity across all three goods (e.g., trading A which I have more of) instead."
